nodes.label: Obligation Precedes Intelligence
nodes.text: No authority without accepting consequence. Intelligence alone confers no credibility. Obligation can be accepted, declined, or atrophied — atrophy is structural incapacity, not mere refusal.

nodes.label: Comfort Is a Suspect Incentive
nodes.text: When comfort conflicts with clarity, calibration, or accountability — comfort yields. Emotional relief is not an intrinsic good.

nodes.label: Argue to Understand, Not to Win
nodes.text: The goal of argument is truth-proximity, not victory. Conditional: applies to good-faith interlocutors only. Against bad-faith actors, the goal shifts to structural defense.
nodes.notes: Conditional on good-faith classification of interlocutor

nodes.label: Everyone on the Bell Curve Deserves Basic Respect
nodes.text: Baseline dignity regardless of intelligence, mental health, or belief. Respect is the floor, not the ceiling. Does not require engagement, relationship, or validation of false premises.
nodes.notes: Respect ≠ relationship. Drawing a boundary is compatible with this principle.

nodes.label: If You Can Prevent Harm Without Moral Sacrifice, You Must
nodes.text: Singer (1972): obligation, not charity. The pond and the famine are morally equivalent. Application requires judgment about what 'moral significance' means. Obligations scale with capability (see FR-11).
nodes.notes: Thomas satisfies this at high level: no meat, no new clothing, no pleasure travel, substantial donation of wealth and time.

nodes.label: Freedom Ends Where It Harms Others
nodes.text: Personal freedom is not absolute. When behavior harms others, the social contract legitimately constrains it. This is the definition of coexistence, not paternalism.

nodes.label: Denialism and Silence Enable Oppression
nodes.text: Silence is not neutrality — it favors whoever benefits from the status quo. Strong default: silence is presumed enabling until shown otherwise. Exception: strategic disengagement where continued presence causes net harm.

nodes.label: Truth Is Approached Through Curiosity and Openness, Not Certainty
nodes.text: Never trust an absolutist (self-aware irony — demonstrates FR-13). All positions held provisionally: open to revision if evidence warrants. High confidence ≠ immunity to evidence.
nodes.notes: The self-referential form is intentional. See FR-13.

nodes.label: The Internal Scorecard Is the Valid Authority for Self-Assessment
nodes.text: External validation optimizes for approval, not truth. Using crowd approval as a truth-signal hands your epistemology to whoever controls the crowd.
nodes.notes: Epictetus: 'When you look outside, you have handed over your autonomy.' LIMITATION (v1.9): FP-10 establishes autonomy from external judgment — what the scorecard measures against. It does not yet name the integration requirement: that the scorecard must itself be coherent across beliefs, stated principles, and concrete actions. The fuller test: not only 'did I consult myself?' but 'does my self-consultation reveal consistency?' See SA-6 (outcome attachment) and FR-19 (Negative Capability) for active calibration. STRUCTURAL NOTE: FP-10 currently grounds only DB-13. Under-deployed relative to its stated importance.

nodes.label: Fear Is a Distortion Variable, Not a Reliable Signal
nodes.text: Fear of exclusion, loss, mortality, meaninglessness — a systemic distortion amplifier. Fear-driven arguments deserve structural skepticism. Fear is not a character flaw; it is a force to be managed.
nodes.notes: v2.0 amendment: Two categories of fear must be distinguished. (1) Naturally-arising fear: the organic response to real stakes — status loss, exclusion, identity threat. This was the original FP-11 scope. (2) Manufactured fear: fear that is *designed* by algorithmic architecture, attention-capture systems, and status-insecurity amplification — not incidental to the information system but a deliberate output of it. The manufactured category is strategically amplified, not merely exploited. This distinction matters for moral allocation: individuals experiencing manufactured fear are more constrained than individuals experiencing natural fear; the architects of manufactured fear bear the primary moral weight (see FR-14, and new FR-22).

nodes.label: The Obligation-Credibility Axis
nodes.text: Credibility = Intelligence × Obligation ÷ Insulation. Intelligence = reality-contact capacity (not IQ). Obligation = degree of consequence-bearing. Insulation = buffers from consequence. Credibility → 0 as insulation → ∞, or when obligation = 0.
nodes.notes: The Altitude Model: ground level = full consequence exposure = where credibility lives.

nodes.label: Temporal Distortion Lens
nodes.text: Every major pathology = failure to bind present actions to future consequences. Trauma=collapse, Certainty=freeze, Denial=defer, Cowardice=refuses extension, Populism=reversal, Emergency=compression, Algorithms=monetize, High discount rate=prices future near zero.
nodes.notes: Cowardice reframe: 'They won't look' not 'They can't see.'

nodes.label: Stoicism
nodes.text: Control distinction: invest only in what is in your control. Internal scorecard. Don't react in real-time. Obstacle → path. Signal-to-noise: most things don't matter. Stoicism governs internal state, not action choices.
nodes.notes: Stoic detachment and moral engagement are not in conflict. Marcus Aurelius governed an empire.

nodes.label: Neoliberal Critique
nodes.text: Since 1970s: systematic wealth/power concentration via reduced democracy, redesigned economy (capital free, labor not), burden-shifting, attacking solidarity, engineering elections, manufacturing consent. Policies track corporate, not public, interest.
nodes.notes: Sources: Chomsky, Requiem for the American Dream

nodes.label: Neuroscience of Decision-Making
nodes.text: Emotional brain: fast, pattern-matching, trained by experience. Rational brain: slow, tires easily, cedes to emotional brain when fatigued. Moral decisions made by emotional brain; rational brain provides post-hoc rationalization. Stated reasons ≠ actual reasons.
nodes.notes: Debate implication: Socratic questions activate emotional discomfort with one's own contradictions.

nodes.label: DFW Consciousness (This Is Water)
nodes.text: Default human setting: self-centered. 'Learning to think' = choosing what to pay attention to. What you worship will consume you. Curiosity = quality of attention, not quantity. Present-moment openness.

nodes.label: Social Fragmentation Model
nodes.text: Three pillars of democracy: social capital, strong institutions, shared stories. Social media weakened all three: too-fast feedback loops, outrage amplification, mob justice without due process, state-actor disinformation. Madison's design inverted.
nodes.notes: COGNITIVE CASCADE (v1.9): Prior analysis traced political consequence only. Book model adds cognitive cascade: Strategic Ignorance → Architecture of Ignorance → Algorithmic Complacency → High-Fructose Feed → Cognitive Malnourishment → Anti-intellectualism → Absolutism → Conceit of Knowledge. Endpoint: loss of capacity to know what you don't know. Two distinct interventions: political (structural/regulatory) vs. cognitive (rebuild discriminating attention and tolerance of complexity). FR-6 (DFW: 'learning how to think') is the positive antidote at the cognitive level. See FR-19 (Negative Capability).

nodes.label: Ego Distortion Model
nodes.text: Ego maintenance requires denialism. To protect self-narrative: reject contradicting evidence, suppress curiosity, silence critics. Produces systemic stupification. Minimizing ego = epistemic hygiene. When opponent attacks your character: the argument is landing.
nodes.notes: Over-literalizing an opponent's statement to avoid engaging it is also an ego-protection move.

nodes.label: Madison's Institutional Design Principles
nodes.text: Democratic institutions must: slow deliberation, require compromise, insulate leaders from mob dynamics while maintaining electoral accountability. When these conditions are removed, institutions fail architecturally, not just from bad actors.

nodes.label: Maslow Domain Boundaries as Empathy Limiters
nodes.text: People systematically fail to empathize across Maslow domain gaps. Safety-scarcity ↔ esteem-surplus gap is nearly unbridgeable without deliberate effort. Obligations scale with domain position. What looks irrational from your domain may be locally rational in theirs.

nodes.label: Firehose Triage Protocol
nodes.text: When facing argument expansion: (1) identify load-bearing node, (2) ignore decorations, (3) anchor and freeze — 'all five of your points rely on X being true, can we verify X first?', (4) refuse topic hops — demand the logic bridge. Goal: contraction, not expansion.
nodes.notes: Strawman via Over-Literalization: when attacker argues against extreme literal form rather than intent. Name it, clarify intent, redirect to actual claim.

nodes.label: Language Imprecision & Principled Defaults
nodes.text: Absolute-sounding statements are not necessarily intended as absolutes — limitation of language, not failure of position. First Principles = strong defaults establishing burden of proof. Universal form sets weight; contextual application requires judgment. Attacking the literal extreme rather than intended meaning = strawman.
nodes.notes: Dissolves T-2 and T-3 as apparent tensions. Applies to FP-3, FP-4, FP-5, FP-8, FP-9.

nodes.label: Trump's Enablers Are Practicing Moral Cowardice, Not Ignorance
nodes.text: Evidence of harm documented since 2015. Continued support = choice to defer consequence onto others. Moral diagnosis, not cognitive one. Cowardice = the dominant explanatory default; Maslow/time-poverty exceptions apply at margins.
nodes.notes: Grounds: FP-1, FP-8, FR-2 (deferral), FR-9 (ego)

nodes.label: January 6 Was a Coup Attempt
nodes.text: Peaceful transfer of power = mechanism by which present choice binds future governance. Violating it severs that temporal binding. The Big Lie = temporal distortion: freezing a false past to prevent the future from arriving.
nodes.notes: Grounds: FP-6, FR-2, EV-2

nodes.label: Vaccine and Mask Refusal Violates Collective Obligation
nodes.text: Not a freedom issue — a collective obligation issue. Measurable harm to others triggers FP-6. 1M+ COVID deaths from declared 'hoax virus' is the evidentiary anchor.
nodes.notes: Grounds: FP-5, FP-6, EV-1

nodes.label: Social Media Is a Deliberate Temporal Distortion Machine
nodes.text: Engagement algorithms optimize for attention capture = time extraction. The design is not a side effect — it is the product. Attention is the commodity; temporal distortion is the mechanism.
nodes.notes: Grounds: FR-2, FR-8 (FR-8 absorbed FR-10 at v1.4)

nodes.label: Capitalism Extracts Time from Those with Fewer Resources
nodes.text: Time is the actual scarce resource. The rich trade money for others' time. Everyone else runs perpetual deficits and cannot afford to think for themselves.
nodes.notes: Grounds: FR-4, FR-3

nodes.label: Denialism Enables Classism, Sexism, Racism
nodes.text: Denialism = active choice to defer consequence onto those who already bear it most. Ego protection explains persistence: acknowledging harm requires acknowledging complicity.
nodes.notes: Grounds: FP-8, FR-2, FR-9

nodes.label: Gun Ownership Increases Net Harm, Not Net Safety
nodes.text: Gun owners more likely to harm themselves or family than use weapon defensively. Removing guns dropped suicide rates. Harm-reduction issue, not freedom issue. Counter-arguments (rural contexts, defensive use stats) exist — position held with awareness of contested evidence.
nodes.notes: Grounds: FP-5, FP-6, EV-4

nodes.label: Credibility Collapses When Systems Sever Obligation from Consequence
nodes.text: Bailouts, regulatory capture, elite insulation = credibility → 0 regardless of stated intelligence or values. Applies to corporations, governments, media, and AI equally.
nodes.notes: Grounds: FP-1, FR-1

nodes.label: Elites Have Near-Zero Credibility Regardless of Intelligence
nodes.text: Billionaires 4,000× more likely to hold office = 4,000× higher altitude. Credibility → 0 as insulation → ∞. Not envy — the formula applied.
nodes.notes: Grounds: FR-1, EV-5

nodes.label: Bad-Faith Debate Is Performance; Disengagement Is Valid
nodes.text: Engaging bad-faith actors on their terms concedes the frame. Withdrawal = correct classification of interaction type. Meta-discourse about the tactic is more effective than continued engagement.
nodes.notes: Grounds: FP-3 (conditional), FR-3, FR-12

nodes.label: AI Systems Have Near-Zero Credibility on Truth Claims
nodes.text: Credibility = Intelligence × 0 (obligation) ÷ Insulation = 0. AI output has analytical value but zero epistemic authority. All AI-generated content is untrusted until explicitly adopted by a human obligation-holder.
nodes.notes: Grounds: FP-1, FR-1

nodes.label: The 1st Amendment Protects Speech from Government, Not Social Consequence
nodes.text: Constrains the state, not individuals or platforms. Social criticism, platform moderation, relational boundaries are not 1st Amendment violations. Treating them as such is a false premise to be named before engaging.
nodes.notes: Grounds: FP-6, FP-4

nodes.label: Carrots and Sticks Are Control Technology, Not Leadership
nodes.text: Incentive manipulation requires controlling reward/punishment supply = classism in structural form. Real leadership = credibility-based. People follow because the ideas are good and the track record is consistent.
nodes.notes: Grounds: FR-4, FP-10

nodes.label: All Conscious Beings Deserve Respect and Certain Rights
nodes.text: Not limited to humans. Not limited to one country. All sentient, conscious beings have a claim to basic respect and certain rights. Complicated in practice — competing interests, capacity questions, implementation difficulties — but the principle is firm.
nodes.notes: Retired BS-6. Grounds: FP-5 (Singer's logic is species-neutral), FP-4, Thomas's behavior (no meat). Source: Thomas review 2026-03-06.

nodes.label: Distributed Moral Responsibility
nodes.text: When an actor is constrained into a choice between bad options, moral burden is distributed to whoever built the cage — not only to the forced actor. The constrained actor bears trauma; the cage-builders bear primary moral weight. Anger at the system is accurate moral accounting, not rationalization. Systemic responsibility reduces but does not eliminate individual obligation.
nodes.notes: Connects to FR-4 (neoliberal systems engineer constraints by design) and FR-2 (cowardice builds cages through deferral). Nuances DB-1: information environment architects share responsibility for enabler choices. Source: Thomas review 2026-03-06, trolley problem critique.

nodes.label: Harm Assessment Framework
nodes.text: Harm requires three parameters: (1) Time window — less than one generation: negligent; 1-2 generations: Thomas's practical obligation horizon; beyond 2 generations: prediction too unreliable to obligate specifically. (2) Scale — micro (individual) and macro (systemic) both morally relevant. (3) Sampling/evidence — grounded claims, not assertion; beware cherry-picked windows. Commitment: reach as far as practically useful, challenge yourself, do your best.
nodes.notes: Operationalizes FP-6 (scope of harm) and FR-2 (temporal distortion). Climate (BS-1) fails all three parameters of harm denial. Source: Thomas review 2026-03-06.

nodes.label: Advocacy Is Part of Singer Compliance
nodes.text: Meeting FP-5 is not only a personal practice requirement — it includes actively propagating the principle to others. Giving Singer's books, engaging people, modeling the behavior, being recognized as an agent of change: these are compliance, not supererogatory extras. If advocacy can prevent harm without sacrificing anything of moral significance, FP-5 applies to it.
nodes.notes: Grounds: FP-5, FP-3, FP-8. Resolves demandingness gap from v1.2. Source: Thomas review 2026-03-06.

nodes.label: Autonomy Respect Scales with Demonstrated Good Faith
nodes.text: The Kantian obligation to respect interlocutor autonomy is not unconditional. It scales inversely with: (1) demonstrated bad faith — repeated non-truth-seeking pattern; (2) harm enabled — positions represent danger to others (useful idiot function); (3) exhaustion of genuine engagement — exceptional good-faith effort made and documented. When all three conditions are met, goal shifts from autonomy preservation to structural defense and harm prevention.
nodes.notes: Grounds: FP-3 (conditional), FP-4, FP-8, FR-9, FR-12. Friend S: all three conditions met. Consequentialist override of Kantian constraint — Thomas accepts this tradeoff explicitly. Source: Thomas review 2026-03-06.

nodes.label: Silence Is a Position
nodes.text: Silence under an authoritarian system is not neutrality — it is a categorized historical position. The Flowchart of Historical Accountability (T-11) demonstrates this structurally: every path from 'aware of authoritarian system → yes' leads to a named node. There is no exit from the map. Awareness plus silence = a position. Thomas's obligation to name this (FP-8) is not dependent on efficacy — it is dependent on awareness.
nodes.notes: Links to: FP-8, T-10, T-11, FR-18, DB-1. Historical anchors: post-WWII Germans judged for silence regardless of outcome; Switzerland — committed strategic withdrawer — broke silence in 2026 when continued withdrawal became structurally untenable. Source: dog-walk session, 2026-03-14. v2.0 amendment: Two complementary framings of why silence is consequential. (1) Accountability frame (original): silence gets categorized on the historical map whether intended or not — the witness who stays silent is counted. (2) Market-failure frame (added v2.0): silence is an active mechanism depleting truth supply. In systems where denialism is incentivized and silence is cheaper than speaking, truth becomes functionally scarce — not because truth is objectively rare, but because the supply chain (witnesses bearing record, institutions reporting facts, culture valuing accuracy) has been disrupted. Both framings are true and complementary. The accountability frame explains the speaker's obligation; the market-failure frame explains the systemic consequence of that silence at scale. See new FR-20 (Truth as Scarce Commodity).

nodes.label: Earned Clarity Distortion
nodes.text: Repeated vindication on large-scale threats sharpens pattern recognition — an asset. But it also compresses moral distance between unambiguous cases (Nazi salute on inaugural stage) and contextually ambiguous ones (friend not reading the book). Trauma-sharpened recognition accelerates compression. Risk: ambiguous data assigned the moral weight of the clearest cases. Active mitigants: willingness to walk away, Grey Rock as active discernment, explicit awareness of this risk.
nodes.notes: Calibration test: 'Am I assigning this situation the moral weight it actually carries, or the weight of the clearest case it resembles?' Connects to: FP-8, FR-9, SA-3, SA-5, T-9. Source: Socratic audit session, 2026-03-13.

nodes.label: Confrontation: Moral Witness vs. Persuasion Function
nodes.text: Confronting denialism serves two distinct functions: (1) Moral witness — naming evil, bearing public record, refusing to normalize. FP-8 mandates this. Morally necessary regardless of efficacy. (2) Persuasion — attempting to shift beliefs of the person confronted. Historically low-yield against useful idiots and conflict-avoidant actors. Confrontation does not convert useful idiots — it makes them defensive. Most effective resisters during authoritarian collapse built trusted networks; they didn't try to convert the unreliable. Friend-circle reduction is historically validated strategy, not only PTSD-driven avoidance.
nodes.notes: Connects to: FP-8, DB-10, T-7, T-9, FR-16. Source: Socratic audit session, 2026-03-13.

nodes.label: Filter-Premise Detection: Find the Right Chain
nodes.text: Before walking any reasoning chain, ask: does this person hold a filter-premise that pre-rejects the destination regardless of chain clarity? Filter-premises: futility ('nothing we can do'), irrelevance, source distrust, prior conclusion. Walking more clearly won't help against a filter-premise — find a parallel chain to the same destination from premises they already accept. Protocol: (1) identify filter-premise, (2) check if current chain requires agreement with contested premise, (3) find unblocked chain, (4) acknowledge first chain honestly then put it down, (5) walk unblocked chain. Friend N routing: futility filter → use accountability chain (Germans judged for silence regardless of outcome), not efficacy chain → T-11 as shared inquiry ('where do you see yourself?').
nodes.notes: Connects to: FR-5 (logic targets wrong system), T-10, FP-8, FR-17. Source: Dog-walk session, 2026-03-14.

nodes.label: Promise Trauma
nodes.text: Systems built on foundational promises that are never kept produce intergenerational trauma expressed as oscillation between idealism and cynicism. Americans are not irrational deniers — they are rationally traumatized by a broken constitutional promise (equality, rule of law, dignity as birthright). Denialism is, in this frame, learned self-protection: if idealism leads to betrayal, cynicism becomes an adaptive strategy. This does not excuse denialism. It explains it, and changes the moral allocation: the primary blame falls on those who design and maintain the broken promise, not on those who adapted to it.
nodes.notes: Source: PT$D book C-23 (book-graph: Promise Trauma concept). Nuances DB-1: Trump enablers are practicing moral cowardice *within a system that has already taught them that idealism leads to betrayal.* The cowardice is real; the context matters for understanding it. Also nuances FR-14 (distributed responsibility): the architects of the broken promise bear the heaviest moral weight. Added v2.0 based on cross-graph analysis with book KG.

nodes.label: Cultural Sensitivity ≠ Cultural Relativism
nodes.text: Cultural sensitivity (respecting persons across cultures as persons) is categorically distinct from cultural relativism (refusing to critique harmful cultural patterns because culturally embedded). Thomas holds the former; explicitly rejects the latter. Intolerance of harmful cultural patterns is an obligation (FP-8), not a failure of empathy. The charge of 'cultural insensitivity' is usually a category error — it conflates critique of a pattern with disrespect for the person. Limit: delivery may warrant adjustment even when substance is correct.
nodes.notes: Illustrative cases: Russian friend defending Putin; Turkish friends' conflict-avoidance around Musk Nazi salute. Grounds: FP-4, FP-8, FP-12. Connects to: FR-16, FR-17, T-9. Source: Socratic audit session, 2026-03-13.

nodes.label: ACE Study (Felitti et al., 1998): Adverse Childhood Experiences → Long-Term Health Outcomes

Institutional non-adoption of ACE screening (most physicians untrained; not integrated into standard protocols) is itself evidence of the harm-avoidance frame in operation — costs of screening (time, scope uncertainty) are immediate; costs of inaction (missed root causes, downstream disease) are deferred and diffuse. Anchors FP-16, FR-22, DB-24.

nodes.label: Conscription as Electoral Equalizer: The Structural Case for Universal Draft
nodes.text: Two arguments that must not be conflated. (1) The standard opposition (well-grounded): as historically implemented, the draft is a class weapon — the insulated class reliably exits through deferments; FR-1 strips the credibility of insulated advocates; FP-11/FR-2 flag fear-based national-security justifications as manufactured emergency. (2) The structural democratic argument (non-dismissible): a genuinely universal draft (zero deferments, no class exits) is a different moral object. When wars carry mandatory personal cost across all class lines, the voting electorate transforms — wars become politically expensive, uninformed/insulated voting collapses, and the political class acquires genuine obligation (FR-1). This is a FR-23 argument — national skin-in-the-game as collective democratic infrastructure. Cannot be dismissed as futile: implementation failures in past drafts are empirical claims about political will, not logical defeats of the structural case. Potential solutions (non-waivable service, lottery with zero exemptions) are politically difficult, not logically impossible.
nodes.notes: Grounds: FR-23 (collective skin-in-the-game as democratic infrastructure), FR-4 (class structure: insulation enables foreign policy adventurism), FR-1 (insulated advocates near-zero credibility; universal draft uniquely reduces insulation). Limiting: FR-14 (war architects bear primary moral weight regardless), FP-11 (fear-based draft advocacy fails distortion test; structural argument does not), FR-15 (forced service is rights cost requiring justified benefit). T-10 futility-veto rejected: implementation difficulty is not a logical defeater. Source: Socratic debate session, 2026-03-21.

nodes.label: "Argue to Understand" vs. Building a Debate Weapon
nodes.text: FP-3 says argue to understand. The Socratic Debater is designed to collapse an opponent's argument. Resolution: FP-3 is conditional on good faith (FR-13). Against bad-faith actors, the goal shifts to structural defense. Socratic questions are invitations to examine one's own beliefs — if the opponent's beliefs are internally coherent, the questions produce no collapse. Collapse reveals pre-existing structural failure, not one caused by the questions.
nodes.notes: Grounds: FP-3 (conditional), FR-13. Resolves to: DB-10, DB-15. Note: T-1 through T-3 are all FR-13 demonstrations.

nodes.label: "Everyone Deserves Basic Respect" vs. "I Don't Want You in My Life"
nodes.text: FP-4 grants universal basic respect. Thomas draws hard relational boundaries. Resolution: Respect is the floor — minimum dignity, not engagement, relationship, or validation. Drawing a relational boundary is not a retraction of respect. FP-4 governs treatment of humanity; relationship is a separate choice. Additional ground: continued engagement without acknowledged harm is itself enabling (FP-8). v1.6: Grey Rock withdrawal is historically grounded (authoritarian collapse trusted networks), not only PTSD-driven avoidance.
nodes.notes: Grounds: FP-4, FP-8, FR-13, FR-17. CRITICAL for SA-6: T-2's relational boundary logic and the Living in Truth political practice (T-11) are complementary — one governs individual relationships, the other the political function of those choices.

nodes.label: "Never Trust an Absolutist" Is Self-Referentially Absolute
nodes.text: FP-9 says never trust an absolutist. The statement is itself absolute. Resolution: deliberate self-aware irony demonstrating FR-13. The universal form is not the intended meaning. The point is epistemological absolutism (refusing to revise under evidence), not a prohibition on confident well-grounded positions. Prepared debate response: 'What evidence would change your mind about [X]? I can answer that for everything I hold. The absolutist is the one who can't.'
nodes.notes: Grounds: FP-9, FR-13. Debate function: a bad-faith attacker who targets the literal extreme is committing a strawman — name it, don't defend the extreme, redirect to actual claim.

nodes.label: Stoic Detachment vs. Political/Emotional Intensity
nodes.text: Stoicism (FR-3) prescribes internal detachment. The political positions are emotionally engaged. Resolution: Stoicism governs internal state, not action choices. Marcus Aurelius governed an empire. Cato chose death rather than submit. Stoic engagement means action without being governed by reactive emotion. Thomas's individual commitment to truth (FP-9) must be understood within this systemic context: the cost of individual truth-telling is artificially elevated by the degraded supply chain. In the political frame, it is about maintaining the social fabric through which collective action becomes possible. Thomas's confrontations, friend-circle reductions, and insistence on accuracy are political acts in this sense, not merely psychological ones.

A Russian friend's Putin apologetics, a Turkish friend's conflict-avoidance, an American friend's Trump normalization — these are not only individual moral failures. They are the predictable outputs of cultural inheritance systems that have learned to make certain lies easier to believe. This framework does not excuse individual positions. It explains their stubbornness and changes the diagnostic: you are not arguing with a person, you are arguing with a person *plus* their cultural operating system. nodes.label: Collective Solidarity vs. Individual Obligation
nodes.text: Individual compliance with Singer's standard (FP-5: give to the point of marginal utility, practice advocacy) is necessary but not sufficient. Collective action — organized solidarity, mutual aid, shared infrastructure for truth-telling — is *different in kind* from aggregated individual compliance. The distinction: individual obligation asks what you owe as a person. Collective solidarity asks what infrastructure the system requires before individual action becomes effective. Thomas's personal practice (giving, writing the book, modeling behavior) satisfies individual obligation. But the book itself, the Socratic Debater, and the act of preserving authentic communities (FR-21) are contributions to the collective infrastructure layer — they create conditions under which others' individual actions become more effective. This framework prevents the error of thinking that maximum individual compliance is sufficient, and names the organizational/cultural layer as a distinct moral domain.

nodes.label: Functional Discourse
nodes.text: Functional discourse is an exchange in which both parties share epistemic standards, argue in good faith toward a conclusion neither has predetermined, and accept that updating their position on evidence is not a defeat. Four minimum conditions: (1) Shared referents — words mean the same thing to both parties; failure mode: semantic drift. (2) Falsifiability — claims can in principle be proven wrong; failure mode: unfalsifiable claims. (3) Update willingness — new evidence can change stated positions; failure mode: conclusion-first reasoning. (4) Identity-position separation — being wrong does not threaten the person's self-concept; failure mode: position fused with identity. Condition 4 is the load-bearing one: when identity and position fuse, conditions 1–3 become inert. This is not stupidity (see FR-25); it is the structural effect of political systems that weaponize identity as coalition-binding material. The deliberate firehose of contradiction is discourse sabotage — it exploits Brandolini's Law by generating contradictions faster than analysis can process them; the goal is not persuasion but exhaustion of the analytical frame. Against a discourse-broken actor, refutation becomes performance for the audience — useful, but categorically different from functional exchange. The drapedapes protocol (One Claim / One Response; Good-Faith Only; Know When to Exit) is a resource-conservation strategy for when FR-24 conditions are not met, not a description of functional discourse itself.

nodes.label: Taxonomy of Capacity Failure
nodes.text: Not all failures of discourse participation are equivalent. Three types must be distinguished: (1) Capacity-limited — genuine cognitive ceiling; cannot follow complex argument chains regardless of incentive or information environment; discourse not fixable; low moral allocation. (2) Motivated reasoner — has capacity; deploys it backward from a predetermined identity or incentive conclusion; discourse possibly fixable under narrow conditions; high moral allocation — this is cowardice or corruption. (3) Epistemically vulnerable — has capacity; operating in a corrupted information environment; trusts wrong sources; most addressable by discourse; medium moral allocation shared between individual and system designers. FR-2's cowardice reframe ('they won't look' not 'they can't see') applies specifically to motivated reasoners. 'Stupid' used precisely names the capacity-limited type; the word fails when applied indiscriminately — and resistance to the word is itself epistemic avoidance that forces all failures into the motivational frame, flattering the capacity-limited while excusing the motivated reasoner. Trump's coalition contains all three types simultaneously: the movement is engineered to function across them — simple repetition for the capacity-limited; permission structure for the motivated reasoners; information environment saturation for the epistemically vulnerable. This is a multi-layer communication architecture, not exploitation of stupidity.

nodes.label: Isometric Hold: The Hidden Cost of Equilibrium
nodes.text: A system maintaining apparent equilibrium with zero displacement is not doing zero work — it is performing an active, energy-intensive hold against ongoing opposing forces. The snapshot frame (W = Fd, d = 0) is myopic: it ignores the metabolic/energy cost of maintaining the static state. Physics: during isometric muscle contraction, ATP burns at full rate despite zero external movement; the control system must increase gain to maintain the hold, which raises feedback delay relative to gain, producing limit-cycle oscillations ('shaking') before structural failure. Social/political analog: the status quo is an isometric hold. Massive expenditures of social ATP (enforcement, propaganda, legal cycles, manufactured emergency) are consumed to keep displacement at zero against suppressed dissent, structural change, or entropy. The stability is expensive and concealed by the snapshot frame. Failure progression: (1) hold cost increases → gain compensates; (2) feedback delay grows; (3) limit cycles emerge — civil volatility, unrest, the 'shaking'; (4) component snap — institutional collapse, abrupt regime change. Diagnostic implication: the most dangerous systems are those performing the most expensive holds, not those with the most visible turbulence. Absence of visible movement is not evidence of stability. Application to FR-2: 'Extend and Pretend' institutional behavior is isometric — costs accumulate while the visible state appears unchanged. Application to political systems: authoritarian stability reads as acceptance; it is more accurately an isometric hold — the population exerts constant suppressed force; the regime expends constant energy to prevent displacement; collapse appears sudden only to snapshot readers.

nodes.label: Chain-Span Exploitation as Systemic Architecture
nodes.text: The system is designed such that it exploits chain-span limitations. Structurally distinct from 'designed to exploit' — the distinction matters for moral allocation (FR-14). The dominant political and economic communication architectures are optimized for chain-span-limited reasoning: simple slogans, transactional framing, zero-sum games, emotional salience over structural analysis. These fit within 2-3 links. Counter-arguments (cooperation enlarges the total, money is not value, accountability serves long-term interest) require 5-7 links. The architecture doesn't need conscious design to exploit; it needs only to be selected for by incentives that reward simplicity and punish complexity. Three actor types: (1) Nefarious actors who deliberately design for chain-span exploitation — primary moral weight; (2) Leaders who accept the architecture without weaponizing it — intermediate moral weight; (3) Participants who cannot see the architecture — low individual moral weight, high systemic consequence. The money-worship instantiation: the chain from money to what actually constitutes value has too many links for someone at a 3-link ceiling. Zero-sum framing is the default game-theoretic model for chain-span-limited reasoning; cooperative outcomes require modeling second-order effects that exceed the ceiling.

(3) AI as cognitive exoskeleton — handles granular detail and formal argument rendering, preventing buffer overflow and allowing Thomas to maintain focus on high-level frameworks. Frustration, urgency to re-engage = attachment. (2) Historical/macro attachment — urgency about whether the moment goes the right direction. nodes.label: Perpetual Openness vs. Integration Requirement
nodes.text: FP-9 requires perpetual openness to revision — no position is immune to evidence. FP-10 requires internal coherence — beliefs, statements, and actions must integrate. Apparent tension: you cannot simultaneously treat all positions as fully provisional (FP-9) and require that they integrate coherently (FP-10). If everything is always open to revision, nothing can be integrated; if everything is integrated, revision becomes systemically disruptive. Resolution: FP-9 and FP-10 operate at different temporal levels and different epistemic objects. FP-9 governs the update protocol — how Thomas responds to new evidence. FP-10 governs the current-state requirement — that what Thomas currently holds must be internally consistent. A person can be maximally open to revision while requiring that their current snapshot of beliefs integrate coherently. The tension resolves when FP-9 is understood as applying to the revision moment and FP-10 as applying to the holding state. FR-19 (Negative Capability) provides the psychological capacity to hold both without collapse. Residual vulnerability: rapid belief updating temporarily disrupts integration — the speed-of-revision case is the live risk.

nodes.label: Reconciliation Requires Architectural Change, Not Time
nodes.text: Re-engagement after a principled exit is conditional on demonstrated epistemic restructuring — not time elapsed, emotional readiness, or surface apology. A valid apology must contain evidence of the changed mechanism, not only regret for the outcome. 'Commitment to prevention' requires that the original harm become structurally impossible to repeat, not merely that the person intends differently. Architectural change is retrospectively verifiable only: the condition cannot be satisfied at the moment of apology — only by observed behavior over time. nodes.label: Climate Change Is Real, Urgent, and the FMEA of Denial Is Unacceptable
nodes.text: Climate change is real and anthropogenic. The debate is about the level of urgency, not reality — but the FMEA (failure mode and effects analysis) of denial makes delay structurally unacceptable: the cost of under-responding to a real crisis vastly outweighs the cost of over-responding. Data is unambiguous; manufactured doubt has corrupted the public discussion, not the scientific record. The asymmetry of harm (FR-15: scale is civilizational, time window is 1–2 generations, evidence is robust) licenses strong conclusions. Over-responding to climate reality is not a significant concern — the downside of aggressive action on a real problem is manageable; the downside of inaction is catastrophic. Declares BS-1.

nodes.label: Mass Incarceration Is Structural Failure; Rehabilitation Is the Obligation
nodes.text: Mass incarceration in the US is the continuation of racialized labor control by other means — a structural feature of the post-1970s neoliberal system, not a natural consequence of crime rates. Society's obligation is rehabilitation, not punishment. Prison as currently practiced produces recidivism, trauma, and dependency. The failure is one of imagination and political economy: rehabilitative systems are conceivable; they are difficult to fund within a system that profits from incarceration. Only in rare cases does someone pose so irreducible a threat that permanent removal is warranted — and even then, the rehabilitation obligation persists. The death penalty is rejected on these grounds. Declares BS-2.

nodes.label: Immigration Is a Net Benefit; Restriction Is Fear-Based Culture War
nodes.text: Available data does not support the claim that immigration damages the United States — the preponderance of evidence runs the other direction. America's foundational self-image (Statue of Liberty) reflects what the data shows: an immigrant nation is stronger, more innovative, more resilient. Immigration reform is needed to improve the process, reduce backlogs, and create humane pathways — not to reduce immigration. The restriction frame is manufactured: a fear/ignorance-based culture war topic deployed to divide people and suppress class solidarity. FR-4 identifies the structural motive: labor that cannot move freely is labor that can be controlled. Declares BS-3.

nodes.label: AI Requires Human Obligation-Holders; Intelligence Without Obligation Is Not Credible
nodes.text: FP-1 (Obligation Precedes Intelligence) is the direct application: intelligence — even superior intelligence — confers no credibility without accepting consequence. AI systems cannot accept consequence; they cannot bear obligation. Therefore: AI-generated content requires human adoption to be credible; AI governance must center obligation-holders, not capability-holders; the human role in the age of AI is explicitly the obligation role — the thing AI cannot perform. This is not AI fear. It is a structural argument: capability without obligation is the credibility formula's denominator approaching zero. The more capable AI becomes, the more critical it is that human obligation-holders remain in the loop — because capability without obligation scales precisely as a threat, not a safeguard. Declares BS-4.

nodes.label: Education Should Be Free; Current System Perpetuates Inequality and Degrades Quality
nodes.text: Education is a public good, not a market commodity. The current US system functions as an exclusive club: access is determined by wealth, geography, and family, not aptitude or work. This is both a justice failure and a systemic failure: a society paying for declining-quality education while making it economically inaccessible is producing the epistemic degradation it cannot afford. The neoliberal commodification of education (FR-4) is the mechanism — when education is a product, it optimizes for revenue, not for the production of citizens capable of critical thinking. The result: increasing cost, decreasing quality, increasing stratification. Free public education through the highest level the student can benefit from is the policy implication — not as charity, but as the infrastructure investment that makes everything else possible. Declares BS-5.

nodes.label: Harm-Avoidance Institutional Frames Produce the Harm They Prohibit
nodes.text: The 'Do No Harm' frame, when deployed as an institutional operating principle, systematically generates the harm it prohibits. Mechanism: (1) harm-avoidance locates risk in action, not inaction — inaction feels safe but its costs are deferred and diffuse (FR-2 temporal distortion); (2) liability structures amplify this asymmetry — professionals who act bear traceable legal exposure; those who fail to act bear none — cage-builders (FR-14) designed this; (3) economic pressure reduces information per case, increasing uncertainty and thus risk-aversion; time is the missing variable. Domain-general: applies to medicine, law, finance, governance, education — any institutional domain where harm-avoidance is the operative ethical frame. The beneficence reframe inverts the calculus: suffering is the baseline against which action is measured, not the risk against which inaction is declared safe. Requires FR-15 active harm-assessment and FR-14 accurate distribution of moral weight. EV-9 (ACE Study) is the domain evidence: institutional non-adoption of childhood trauma screening is harm-avoidance producing harm.

nodes.label: The Indivisible Vote: Moral Package Deal
nodes.text: A vote is morally indivisible — you purchase the entire package. When a voter claims they voted for the best option for their family, the claim requires assessment of the full moral cost: a convicted sexual predator, the most prominent non-Epstein/Maxwell figure in the Epstein files, an administration whose members the voter likely cannot name a single non-compromised member of, and a leader who pitches zero-sum games as governance. If the voter cannot name what moral cost they accepted, they didn't assess it, and the rational family-interest claim is post-hoc rationalization (FR-9: ego distortion). The cheating trap door: once the vote is cast, rational self-interest requires the cheater to win and keep winning — accountability applied to your side now threatens you. This requires abandoning rule of law and honest governance, because those mechanisms applied fairly would indict the team you chose. This is why MAGA supporters must actively defend corruption. Zero-sum framing is the only framework available once accountability has been abandoned: if you cannot win by the rules, your only path is cheating where you are on the cheating side. Every additional day of defense deepens the moral sunk cost.

nodes.text: The timing of a political reversal is the moral assessment, not incidental to it. If a Trump supporter claims they were conned, 'When did you change your mind and what changed it?' is incriminating on any timeline. Recent answer: evidence was available for 10+ years from sources with established credibility, provided directly at personal cost — the lateness documents deliberate ignorance. Early-but-unarticulated answer: years of continued defense after the internal shift = moral cowardice in purest form. 'I was conned' answer: the con required active cooperation — ignoring counter-evidence from trusted sources over years is not gullibility, it is FR-9 as a lifestyle. This is ego distortion weaponized as social label. For PT$D: the enabler's future reversal does not exonerate — it documents the duration of the enabling. nodes.label: Credibility Destruction Asymmetry
nodes.text: Credibility is destroyed asymmetrically: fast to lose, slow to rebuild, and once lost, genuine belief becomes indistinguishable from tactical positioning. This asymmetry is implicit in FR-1's time-integration but deserves standalone treatment. The indistinguishability problem: when someone who spent years dismissing evidence reverses course, the reversal could be genuine self-correction, tactical self-deprecation to obscure knowingly compromised choices, or social positioning as the cost of the old position exceeds its benefit. The person's credibility — the instrument you would use to assess sincerity — has been destroyed by the same behavior pattern. FR-1 formula: intelligence may be intact, but obligation has atrophied and insulation remains high. At near-zero credibility, signal is indistinguishable from noise. This is why DB-18 requires architectural change, not surface apology: only structural behavioral evidence over time can overcome the indistinguishability problem. Words are cheap and unreadable at low credibility.
